container.$comment: A reading column. The component is one sentence of CSS — centre a capped column and pad its sides — and both numbers live here so a page-wide rhythm is a theme decision, not a per-page copy. It also declares `container-type: inline-size`, which costs no token: what it buys is that everything inside can respond to THIS column with a container query instead of guessing at the viewport.
container.$comment-max-width: The cap of the column. 72rem is 1152px at the default root size — wide enough for a three-card grid with air, narrow enough that a line of running text inside a half-column still lands near a readable measure. In rem on purpose: a reader who raises the root font size widens the column with the type instead of cramming more letters into the same pixels.
container.$comment-padding-x: The gutter between the column and the screen edge. A clamp, because the gutter is the one length that genuinely follows the viewport: tight on a phone where every pixel is content, generous on a desktop where a hard edge looks unfinished. The floor is the spacing scale's 16px step; the ceiling is a measured 40px, past which the gutter reads as empty margin rather than as breathing room.
